subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should portable agent bundles be a first-party core import/export feature, a plugin/ClawHub bundle format backed by new core APIs, or folded into the existing backup/migration roadmap?
rationale: The answer determines CLI namespace, manifest schema, overwrite semantics, secret/session exclusions, plugin API scope, and how this avoids conflicting with existing backup and migration work.

options.title: Scope a first-party bundle contract
options.body: Define a core preview/dry-run import/export contract for non-secret agent config, workspace files, skills, env requirements, and bindings before any implementation PR.

options.title: Route through plugin APIs and ClawHub
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only missing agent-registration/import APIs and let ClawHub packages own optional portable agent bundles.

options.title: Merge into backup/migration design
options.body: Treat agent bundles as a mode of the broader backup or migrate work so archive trust, restore, and path-remap policy stay in one product surface.

recommendation.title: Scope a first-party bundle contract
recommendation.body: Define a core preview/dry-run import/export contract for non-secret agent config, workspace files, skills, env requirements, and bindings before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The local history shows broad recent work across agent CLI, gateway file handling, and docs, making this the best available cross-surface routing candidate.
